But on the other hand, when the going gets tough, humor turns into a life jacket that keeps us from inking. People like fun and amusement. Our sense of humor tells others that we are easy to be with and open to all kinds of interaction. In school, a happy and interactive class is open to new ideas and umorous ice- breakers always warm up students. In the workplace, it is humor that keeps the atmosphere light during stressful situations. Also, people who have shared laughter together share a special bond about their relationship. When we are children, we have no difficulty bringing laughter into our lives. We laugh at everything and we play for mere pleasure. As we grow and mature, we slowly cheat ourselves out of the child within us. As a result, our desire for humor and laughter is constant and we try whatever we can to get the lost pleasures of childhood back. It is possible for each one of us to be humorous, but we must have a burning desire to be so. You must want to make others happy as well, just like a humorist. Agood humorist learns to interact with his audience. He produces laughter and excitement in the audience. Then he leans back, making as if to let the audience take over. Next he would pretend that it is not he that makes them laugh but they laugh of their own accord. Pretty amazing, isn’t it? Still, what matters most is your intention to be humorous.
What is the purpose of this passage?
options: To prove that an air of humor in the workplace can reduce stress.
To show how humor has developed throughout the history of mankind.
To suggest that a sense of humor be developed as early as months old.
To explain why humor is important and what one can do to be humorous.

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about a humorist?
options: He tries to help the audience recall why they are not as cheerful as they used to be.
He makes the audience feel that they cannot but laugh and no one else makes them do so.
He chooses to work in a company where there is humorous interaction among people.
He often wears a life jacket so as to produce laughter and excitement in the audience.

questions.text: What does the expression “the going gets tough” in the first paragraph most likely mean?
options: Health is wealth.
Nothing goes wrong.
Conditions become difficult.
Something nice happens.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT discussed in this passage?
options: Why people enjoy being with a humorous person.
What makes the atmosphere enjoyable in the workplace.
How a humorist does his best to make the audience laugh.
Where the most interactive class in the world can be found.

questions.text: Which of the following words best describes the overall tone of this passage?
options: Cruel.
Encouraging.
Doubtful.
Upset.
